name: Evaluating Text-to-Video Alignment: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Video Generation Models
description: In the area of video generation, text-to-video (T2V) alignment refers to the critical ability of producing content that is consistent with textual descriptions. Despite the development of various T2V methods, there is still a lacks of a systematic evaluation benchmark to comprehensively assess their alignment ability. In this study, we propose a hierarchical and multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark, with the aim to complement the shortcomings of existing evaluation protocols and consequently improve the video generation quality with respect to T2V alignment. The benchmark categorizes T2V alignment ability into four tiers-fundamental, action, relational, and temporal-covering a total of 13 evaluation dimensions. Coupled with 542 rigorously selected evaluation prompts and the automated binary scoring of Gemini 1.5 Pro, the proposed benchmark offers a comprehensive and objective assessment of T2V alignment. Experimental results demonstrate that the benchmark proposed in this study achieves an average Pearson correlation 69% compared with human judgments.
reputation: New hierarchical suite for text-to-video alignment with early adoption in the video-generation evaluation community.
notes: Relies heavily on human judgments (subjective) and may supplement with automated metrics (e.g., CLIP-based scores); evaluation can be small-scale and costly; automatic metrics are imperfect proxies for alignment.
